findings.summary: The [[maybe_unused]] detection was dead. `new RegExp(` ${name} `)` in a template literal builds a BACKSPACE-delimited pattern, not a word boundary, so it matched nothing and every named callback parameter was annotated regardless. Traced live into generated/scene157/main.cpp, which annotated a parameter the next line reads, and measured at 44,285 wasted RegExp constructions per corpus compile. The scan is gone and the parameter is annotated unconditionally, which is what the sibling compileNamedFrameCallback already did and is byte-identical to what shipped.

Three angles said to replace the hand-rolled mutation guard with Compiler.inferredObjectIsMutated. Tried, and it refused the feature: that function answers "is this object's identity observable", so storingDataMethods contains "set" and scene 174's `agentBox.scaling.set(agentParams.radius * 2, ...)` marks agentParams mutated through a whole-subtree alias test. Correct for reference storage, wrong for "is the literal still the value". The guard stays purpose-built, with the reviews' specific weaknesses fixed instead.

That guard's scope walk used a hand-rolled function-kind list, so a `const` inside a METHOD climbed past it and scanned the whole file; it also missed ++/--, delete, and the load-bearing case. It now uses ts.isFunctionLike and refuses a bag passed to a call that reaches a BODY -- which distinguishes an intrinsic, declared in a .d.ts with nothing to inline, from scene-local code this compiler inlines with an object parameter bound by reference.

Its doc comment justified the guard with `const casters = [x]` followed by push -- a case the object-literal check one line above makes unreachable -- and claimed to be "conservative by construction" while catching only two of five write shapes. Rewritten to cite a reachable case and to say what it actually decides.

Four doc comments were orphaned by inserting declarations at grep anchors: the 14-line findClosestPoint block came to document navigation_compute_path, and the CrowdAgent.position block to document agentGoto, in both the PAL header and its source. The declarations moved below the functions their preceding comments describe.

The lowerer claimed the pin's pre-snap is not redundant because it runs at _tmpHalfExtents -- but that is the same +-1 as the query default. The pre-snap IS non-redundant, because findClosestPoint is findNearestPoly PLUS closestPointOnPoly and projects the endpoint onto its polygon first. The comment now says the true reason.

agentGoto decided the pin's optional-chain no-op inside the PAL, where its own sibling navigation_agent_position reports absence and lets generated get_agent_position decide what it means. The PAL now returns bool and the generated half owns the Babylon decision; a null-query branch no pinned line motivates is gone.
findStraightPath's flag and polygon-reference outputs are [opt] in Detour's own header and nothing read them -- roughly 2.3 KB allocated per call to be discarded. Both dropped for nullptr.

The include-all dtQueryFilter was built twice with the same two setters. One include_all_filter() beside the half-extents constant now serves the plugin and the crowd retarget, so a future exclude reaches every query rather than the ones someone remembered.

emitDataVectorOfStructs took the loop variable AND a field map whose values embedded it, with nothing checking they agreed. It now mints the name and hands it to a callback, reuses DataLowerer.dataTypeAt, calls the extracted DataLowerer.structAggregate rather than making a fourth copy of the reference-vs-value fork, and reserves -- the pattern that file emits at four other sites.

Gate and registry hygiene: the header numbered its probes against the body's reading order, two corners were resolved by getClosestPoint twice, `settled` named a state the run never reaches, two dataset keys nothing reads, a paragraph recording a cut off-mesh probe, and 90 steps unexplained (it is 1.5 s, which at maxSpeed 1.5 over the diagonal leaves the agent mid-path). Scene 171's registry comment was a fifth copy of one fact and is now a pointer, as 174's already was.

The createNavMesh refusal covered two option names with one reason clause that explained only doNotReverseIndices; expectedLayersPerTile now refuses with its own reason. The off-mesh defaults were stated in three places and are now the PAL header's contract alone.

Measured and dismissed rather than assumed: the mutation scan runs FOUR times per full-corpus compile (0.0055% of compile time, the object-literal check dropping 36,818 of 36,822 candidates), and computePath, agentGoto and the off-mesh packing are all setup-time, called once per scene before the frame loop. No cache and no pooling warranted.
